Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the sample promptset. Putting a short proposal below so we can iterate quickly.

Proposed acceptance gates (pre-canary / canary / full):
1) Quality gate (eval set):
   - A/B acceptance: when model_variant_A (baseline) vs model_variant_B (candidate) has a statistically significant win on the primary metric (user rating) with at least +3% lift and p<0.05 on the 1k prompt subset.
   - Hallucination rate: reductions (or no increase) in factual hallucinations measured by the Acme annotation rubric; delta <= 0.5% allowed.
2) Latency/Cost gate:
   - P95 generation latency <= 600ms for the typical prompt distribution (measured in canary region).
   - Unit token cost within 10% of baseline or documented trade-off approved by Acme.
3) Safety/Regulatory checks:
   - No failing items on the safety checklist (list attached in the shared Drive link).
4) Operational rollback triggers (auto/manual):
   - Automatic rollback if weekly user-rated satisfaction drops by >5% at p<0.05, or if error-rate spikes >2x for more than 30m.

Canary proposal:
- Cohort: 5% of traffic for 48 hours (start-of-day Monday), expand to 20% after 72h if metrics stable.
- Monitoring: token-level cost, per-prompt quality sample (50 prompts/hour sampled and annotated), latency buckets, and user-facing error rate.
- Owner: Redwood infra (Dev) for rollout; Acme product (Sarah) for annotated quality checks.

Next steps: Dev — can you validate the rollback trigger feasibility and add the observability hooks? Marissa — can you confirm customer acceptance process and whether Acme needs a signed SLA change for the pilot?

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical notes and a couple of constraints from infra:

1) Rollback triggers: we can wire automated rollbacks for sharp error-rate spikes and for a simple satisfaction metric (signal from annotated sample). We will need a "grace period" flag to avoid thrashing on noisy signals (suggest 1 hour evaluation window before auto-rollback).

2) Monitoring hooks: we’ll push a dedicated canary dashboard with the following streams: request latency (p50/p95/p99), model variant split, sampled prompt trace (raw prompt + model output), per-prompt annotation link, and token cost.

3) Warmup / prefix caching: to bring p95 down we recommend a short warmup period and pre-warming KV cache for the 5% cohort prior to traffic shift. That adds ~10-15m operational prep.

4) Quantization / variant test: if Acme is sensitive to unit cost, we can include a quantized candidate in the canary. Expect a small quality delta; suggest a separate A/B subtest inside the canary.

I ran an isolated canary yesterday on the provided sample and attached the initial run summary. Nothing catastrophic — main observation is a small uptick in generation time for long-form prompts under the quantized variant.

attachments: canary_run_results-20260511.pdf

Questions for Sarah / Marissa:
- Do you want the canary in us-west only or across regions? (us-west preferred for low-latency sample)
- Compute budget: can we assume the pilot is covered under the existing reserved pool or do we need an explicit commit?

—Dev

Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

2) Communication plan: if we do a rollback, customer-facing comms need to be pre-approved. I can draft a short comms template for product vs. ops.

Timeline note: Acme asked for a pilot confirmation by May 20 so they can schedule an internal Q/A demo. If we want to hit that date, we should start the canary prep this week (warmup scripts and dashboard).

Team + Sarah — thanks for the quick turn. Finalizing the plan below and calling out owners / timelines so we can close the loop before Acme’s May 20 demo.

Actionable acceptance checklist (must pass to proceed to 20% traffic):
- A/B quality: candidate must show >= +3% on primary user rating over baseline on the 1k holdout set, p<0.05 (Owner: Acme + Redwood analytics) — target date: 2026-05-17 EOD
- Hallucination delta <= 0.5% vs baseline on Acme rubric (Owner: Acme annotators) — target: 2026-05-17 EOD
- P95 latency <= 600ms (Owner: Dev / infra) — target: 2026-05-17 EOD
- No safety checklist failures (Owner: Laura) — target: 2026-05-16 EOD
- Observability & dashboard live (Owner: Dev) — target: 2026-05-15 noon
- Comms template + rollback playbook (Owner: Marissa) — target: 2026-05-16 noon

Operational canary schedule:
- Start: 2026-05-18 09:00 PDT at 5% for 48 hours.
- Expand to 20% after 72 hours if all gates green.
- Auto-rollback windows: 1hr evaluation window before any auto-rollback. Manual rollback available to ops at any time.

I’ll mark owners in the shared Drive and we’ll do a short sync Thursday to confirm the dashboard and sample annotations. If any of the owners cannot hit their targets, call it out in-thread ASAP so we can either shift timeline or provide support.

Thanks,
Jonas

Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
